subject.title: California — Proposition 1 (Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs)

positions.statement: Prop 1 - No Recommendation - would issue $11.25 billion in bonds to fund the Multifamily Housing Program, CalVet Home Loan Program, youth housing, and housing for homeless people. … We leave it up to you to decide.

subject.title: California — Proposition 2 (Increases State's Rainy Day Fund)

positions.statement: Prop 2 - YES - would increase the Budget Stabilization Account (BSA) (the Rainy Day Fund) cap from 10% of general fund revenue to 20% and exclude deposits into the BSA from the Gann limit.

subject.title: California — Proposition 3 (Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes)

positions.statement: Tax the Rich for Human Need:  Vote YES on Propositions 3 and 40!

subject.title: California — Proposition 4 (Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns)

positions.statement: Proposition 4 - YES - would allow the state and local governments to create programs that provide candidates with public funds under spending limits and eligibility rules.

subject.title: California — Proposition 5 (Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers)

positions.statement: Proposition 5 - YES - would change the way recalled state officers are replaced.

subject.title: California — Proposition 37 (Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes)

positions.statement: Proposition 37 - NO - Bonds for second mortgages - would establish a second mortgage homebuyer program for some homebuyers on newly constructed homes only and issue $25 billion in bonds to fund the program.

subject.title: California — Proposition 38 (Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research)

positions.statement: Proposition 38 - NO - would issue bonds to establish an Immunology and Immunotherapy Research Institute affiliated with the University of California.

subject.title: California — Proposition 39 (Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification)

positions.statement: Proposition 39 - NO - would require voters to present government-issued identification and require election officials to use government data to confirm voter citizenship and report verification rates.

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.statement: Tax the Rich for Human Need:  Vote YES on Propositions 3 and 40!

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: Vote NO on Propositions 41 and 42. Placed on the ballot by billionaires, these measures would cancel the billionaires’ tax even if proposition 40 passes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.statement: Vote NO on Propositions 41 and 42. Placed on the ballot by billionaires, these measures would cancel the billionaires’ tax even if proposition 40 passes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: Proposition 43 - NO - would require supermajorities for local initiatives to enact taxes whose proceeds are dedicated to a specified purpose. Supermajority requirements are undemocratic.

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.statement: Proposition 44 - YES - would prohibit federally-qualified healthcare clinics from spending less than 90% of their annual revenue on mission-related purposes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: Vote NO on Proposition 45. Proposition 45 changes the California Environmental Quality Act, taking a sledgehammer to environmental review of and public comments about most land use and public works projects.
